newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice market slows ahead of new harvest.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice market slows ahead of new harvest.

text.p: Vietnam's export rice market has been quiet this week as traders await clearance of existing contracts and harvesting of the new crop in the Mekong Delta, dealers said on Thursday.
They said activity on Vietnam's rice market had slowed over the past week or two as stocks from the winter-sping crop petered out.
One added that business was not expected to pick up significantly before the end of this month when the next harvest in the Mekong Delta, the main producing area, is due.
Five percent broken grade was quoted at around $255 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, close to levels a week ago. Ten percent broken was quoted at $250 per tonne.
Despite the quiet, some 20 vessels were reported in Saigon Port at present, with shipments loading for Iraq, West Africa, Cuba and North Korea.

Thursday's Saigon Times Daily quoted trade ministry sources as saying 188,000 tonnes were exported during the first 13 days of July, bringing the total so far this year to just over two million tonnes.
It said trade had slowed recently because dealers were concerned about the impact of the currency crisis in Southeast Asia on Thailand's rice export activities.
